message.text: I've confirmed there's no cron scheduler integrated into the server startup process—the only background job actually running is the S3 presign runner on a 12-hour cycle. The internal scheduler package isn't being used in production, so there's no nightly cleanup job to worry about.

r03.

**Premise correction:** There is no nightly database-cleanup job, and the cron scheduler package is never wired into the running server at all.

The repository does contain a generic cron/scheduler package at `internal/scheduler/` (`scheduler.go`, `job.go`, `parser.go`, `middleware.go`), but a repo-wide search shows it is referenced only from within its own package's tests (`internal/scheduler/example_test.go`, `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go`) and its doc comments (`internal/scheduler/doc.go`) — there is no call to `scheduler.New(...)` or any job registration anywhere in `server/`, `cmd/`, or `store/`. It is unused, dead-code infrastructure, not something actually started at server startup.

Separately, I searched for any database-cleanup/vacuum/nightly job under other names ("cleanup", "cron", "vacuum", "database cleanup") in the production server code and found none. The only background jobs actually wired into server startup (`Server.startBackgroundRunners` in `server/server.go:153-174`) are:

- the S3 presign runner (`server/runner/s3presign`), which runs once at startup and then every **12 hours** (see [h01](h01)) — not a nightly/database-cleanup job, and not driven by a cron expression.

There is no scheduled "nightly" job and no database-cleanup job anywhere in the codebase, so there's no run time to report.
